chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Musa ibn Umar from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Dawud ibn Kathir al-Raqi who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about the meat of the Bakhit (a type of camel) and its milk, so he said: 'There is no harm with it, and this report does not contradict this news.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm with it (permissible)
key_terms.لُحُومِ الْبُخْتِ: Meat of the Bakhit (a specific type of camel)
key_terms.وَلَا يُنَافِي هَذَا الْخَبَرَ: And this report does not contradict this news

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the meat and drinking the milk of the Bakhit camel in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the fiqh of consuming camel products from the 'Bakhit' (often identified as the Bactrian or two-humped camel) by affirming the permissibility of both its meat and milk. The Imam’s addition that this ruling does not contradict other reports (*la yunafi hadha al-khabar*) addresses potential juristic concerns regarding conflicting narrations on camel varieties, reinforcing the principle of *tawqi* (divine authorization) in dietary laws. It highlights the Shia scholarly approach to resolving apparent discrepancies in *akhbar* through precise contextualization.
